Playbook.name: Windows — Query Registry using Built-in Tools - SOC Playbook

ExecutiveSummary.Overview: A host queried the registry via reg.exe query or PowerShell registry access for the first time in the baseline window (new_terms) - reconnaissance of stored configuration/credentials. Triage question: is this attacker registry recon, or normal admin/software activity?
ExecutiveSummary.BusinessImpact: Registry queries can reveal stored credentials, installed security products and configuration an attacker uses to plan the next step.

TelemetryRequirements.Requirement: Windows Security + Sysmon + PowerShell logs via Elastic Agent (verified live). Sysmon event.code 1=process(command_line/parent populated), 11=file, 13/12=registry(registry.path populated); process.code_signature NOT collected.

Signal.Name: Registry query
Signal.Details: reg query / PowerShell registry read, first-seen entity.

InitialAssessment.Rule: Weigh the evidence story, not any single fact - see ClassificationGuidance.

Investigation.Goal: Determine whether the registry query is attacker reconnaissance or benign admin/software activity.

Step.name: What registry paths were queried and by whom
Step.Purpose: Queries of credential/security-product keys by a suspicious parent are recon; software config reads are benign.
Step.Query: FROM logs-windows.sysmon_operational-*,logs-system.security-* | WHERE event.code IN ("1","4688") AND host.name == "$hostname" AND process.command_line IS NOT NULL AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | EVAL cl = TO_LOWER(process.command_line) | WHERE (process.name RLIKE "(?i)reg(.exe)?" AND cl LIKE "*query*") OR (process.name RLIKE "(?i)(powershell|pwsh).*" AND cl LIKE "*hklm:*") | KEEP @timestamp, process.name, process.parent.name, process.command_line, user.name | SORT @timestamp DESC | LIMIT 20
Step.AnalystNotes: Queries of Winlogon/LSA/credential-provider/security-product keys by a script or unusual parent = recon. Reads of an app's own config keys by that app are benign. Note the parent.

Step.name: Process origin and account on the host
Step.Purpose: The parent process and account reveal whether this was interactive attacker activity or an automated/service context.
Step.Query: FROM logs-windows.sysmon_operational-*,logs-system.security-* | WHERE event.code IN ("1","4688") AND host.name == "$hostname" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 2 hours | STATS runs = COUNT(*), parents = VALUES(process.parent.name), users = VALUES(user.name) BY process.name | SORT runs DESC | LIMIT 15
Step.AnalystNotes: A suspicious process spawned by an office app/browser/script interpreter, run by a normal user, is more concerning than one under a known admin/automation parent.

Node.Condition: Registry queries of credential/security-product keys by a suspicious parent, or part of broader discovery.
New registry query with unclear intent.

DocumentationChecklist.Item: Attach outputs of INV-01-REGQUERY-DETAIL, INV-02-PROC-TREE to the case.

FalsePositive.Definition: Normal admin or software configuration access.

SOCAction.Item: Confirm; close as benign_activity; new_terms learns the entity.
Investigate the parent/host; correlate with other discovery; open IR if warranted.

Misconfiguration.Definition: A monitoring/inventory tool reading the registry.

Phase.name: Immediate Actions (0-30 minutes)
Phase.Action: Confirm the activity on the host; if malicious indicators, isolate the host.
Identify the responsible account/process and its origin.

Phase.name: Containment and Eradication (hours)
Phase.Action: Isolate the host; capture volatile evidence; hunt the same pattern across the estate.
Reset credentials used on the host if compromise is confirmed.

Phase.name: Recovery and Hardening (days)
Phase.Action: Remediate the root cause; add/verify EDR coverage; apply relevant hardening.

QualityChecks.Check: Confirm the required telemetry (Sysmon/Security auditing) is present on the host.
Tune known-benign administrative sources via exceptions, not by disabling the rule.

TruePositiveClosure.Item: Host contained and triaged; root cause eradicated; estate swept; findings recorded.
